rows.description: Every place reminds you of them and you cry without warning. Wise: this is real grief, so sleep, eat, move and talk. Immature: numbing with distractions or rushing into a rebound.

rows.subtype: Ex-partner × Sharing private images or messages [Receiver]
rows.description: Fear that an ex will leak private material. Wise: it is a crime and not your shame, so keep evidence and report to the cyber cell or a trusted adult. Harmful: bearing it alone.
Months later you can think of them without hurt. Wise: take lessons about your patterns and needs, without rewriting the past as all bad or all good. Immature: swearing off love.
You replay how they wronged you and feel bitter. Wise: allow anger as information, then let it go for your own peace. Harmful: spreading their private matters or turning friends against them.
Balances career, spouse and care duties, splits tasks with siblings and keeps the parent's dignity.

My ageing parent refuses help, skips medicines, or resents advice and I feel frustrated and worried. I respect their dignity, offer choices, not orders, and involve their doctor or a trusted relative rather than fighting every day.
Carries childhood hurt while caring for them; can provide care and hold boundaries while processing the past, possibly with support.

I live far from my parents for work and feel guilty for not being there. I stay in regular contact, arrange practical support, and make honest visits; guilt is useful when it moves action and harmful when it just torments.
I saw it and did nothing and now feel ashamed. Wise: check on the target privately, report to a teacher, and refuse to laugh. Small acts matter.
After the bully apologises I feel mixed: relief, doubt, anger. Wise: accept the apology without forgetting, keep boundaries, and take time. Forgiving is not the same as trusting again.
I look down on someone weaker and see them as fair game. Wise: challenge that story; it is a fear of being weak myself. Harmful: turning contempt into a public habit.

I hate the person who torments me and picture hurting them. Wise: feel that anger as a sign of harm done, share it with someone safe, and seek adult intervention. Harmful: retaliating, which can put me at risk.
I go to the station to report a theft and hope that they will help. Wise: bring documents, stay respectful, get a copy of the complaint. Harmful: expecting everything to go wrong and not trying.

After an unfair fine or harassment I feel furious and helpless. Wise: record calmly, pursue complaint channels, and channel anger into action rather than confrontation. Harmful: heated words that turn a bad situation into worse.
My friend asks me to lie to the police about where he was. Wise: loyalty does not mean false statements; help him find a lawyer instead. Harmful: perjury that pulls me in with him.

An officer asks me for money or presses me to sign a paper I have not read. Wise: do not sign what I do not understand, ask for a lawyer or a family member, and note names and numbers. Harmful: panicking and complying.
They say if you loved them you would. Wise: you decide your pace; someone who respects you accepts a no. Harmful: giving in out of fear of losing them. Talk to a trusted friend if pressure continues.
You are asked for private photos. Wise: once sent, control is gone; you can refuse without guilt. Harmful: sending under pressure or threats. If threatened, tell an adult and report.
You are told no or not yet and feel hurt. Wise: say thank you for the honesty, step back, and do not sulk or bargain. Harmful: punishing them with coldness or threats.
You want closeness and must ask and listen, not assume. Wise: consent is clear, freely given and can change; a hesitation or silence is not a yes. Harmful: pressure, guilt or persistence.
On my first day I cry as Mummy leaves, then the teacher takes my hand and shows me the toys. I feel scared then a little safe. A warm, steady teacher makes school feel like a friendly place.
I look at the other children and wonder who will be my friend. I feel shy and curious. A wise teacher pairs children for an activity so friendships can begin easily.
I hold on to Mummy's dress and cry at the school gate. Separation is truly hard. Wise parents say a short kind goodbye, tell when they will return and do not sneak away. Lingering makes it harder.
